thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: inference-service request-queue depth > 1k and elevated 5xxs. severity=high. on-call: @maria. channel=#eng-oncall

maria: I'm oncall and looking. Customers reporting long tails — some requests 30-45s. Frontend shows surge of 503/504.

raj: jumping in. which pool? any recent deploys?

maria: no deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot. Affected pool: gpu-pool-us-west-shared. dashboard: pool_util=99% and queue depth trending up.

sophie: pulling the exporter metrics now. short dump: `request_queue_depth=1358, pending_warmups=72, avg_init_time=12.3s`

leo: HPA is at maxreplicas. ran `kubectl get hpa -n inference`; copy below:
```
NAME                 REFERENCE         TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-deploy     Deployment        110%/80%        4         60        60
```
leo: replicas=60 (max). cluster has no spare GPU nodes to schedule additional pods.

kyle: pool-manager logs show many warmups stuck in PENDING because nodes are at capacity and kube-scheduler can't bind pods. Also seeing evictions retrying. snippet:
```
[2034567921] pool-manager: warmup request id=wm-87 state=PENDING reason='no-sched'
[2034567932] scheduler: binding failed: Insufficient GPUs
[2034567945] pool-manager: retry warmup id=wm-87
```

maria: preliminary hypothesis: autoscaling (HPA) already hit max replicas; cluster-level resource shortage prevents scheduling, so warmups queue up which delays readiness and increases queue depth -> 503s.

raj: alternative hypothesis: model init spikes due to KV-cache cold misses after a rolling maintenance earlier; warmup time doubled causing backlog even though replicas exist. any recent cache flush events?

sophie: I see a cache-invalidator event 18m ago from ops-bot: 'manual cache clear for version rollout'. correlates with start of increased avg_init_time.

ops-bot: NOTE: cache-invalidator ran by @infra-team at ts=2034566000 for rollout v12.4.

maria: ok that matches. so two compounding factors: HPA at max + cache cold starts increasing init time + cluster resource exhaustion.

leo: collecting scheduler events and kubelet logs for the time window 2034565800-2034568200. will upload snippets.

sophie: sharing traces from request-router showing where time is spent:
```
- request queued: 1.2s
- routed to pod: 0.5s
- pod init (if warmup pending): 14.7s
- model load: 10.2s
- inference compute: 0.3s
```

kyle: infra note: autoscaler for GPU nodes (nodepool-autoscaler) has a cooldown and is throttled by cloud quota limits. We've hit GPU quota in the region.

maria: live mitigations: 1) toggle fallback routing to smaller CPU-backed model for low-priority traffic, 2) enable emergency burst to dedicated-reserved pool (if policy allows), 3) increase serving timeouts to reduce 503s for clients while we stabilize. I'm going to execute (1) now.

maria: `/runbook route-fallback --priority=low --model=cpu-small-v2` executed. router-bot: routing rule applied, estimated reduction in queue = ~20%.

raj: initiating customer impact callout. list of affected customers? sophie, can you compile a short impact table (org, %errors, start_ts)?

sophie: quick list: org-alpha: 15% error rate since 2034567000; org-beta: 8% since 2034567400; several small customers at 2-5%.

maria: notifying SRE on-call for quota exec: @kyle please open cloud quota request with urgency.

kyle: opened support ticket with cloud provider: ticket#CP-88912. ETA from provider unclear. requesting immediate quota increase.

ops-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: mitigation=route-fallback by maria; ticket=CP-88912 by kyle; followup=warmup tuning by raj.

raj: next steps for RCA thread: we need timeline (assemble scheduler events, cache-invalidator timestamp, HPA metrics, pool-manager warmup queue), hypothesis scoring, and long-term fixes. I'll own the timeline. assigning warmup tuning to @kyle and cache/rollout hygiene to @sophie.

maria: quick fix (2) try dedicated-reserved burst: requesting approval from infra lead, pinging @ops-lead.

leo: uploading extracted scheduler events now: S3 link (private): https://s3.redwood/prod/rca/2034567890/scheduler.txt

sophie: uploading request traces and init time histograms: https://s3.redwood/prod/rca/2034567890/traces.json

maria: current status: queue depth=912 (down from 1358 after fallback), pool_util=96%, pending_warmups=42. still elevated but improving.

kyle: warmup tuning suggestion: prioritize recycling idle GPUs for warmups, reduce warmup concurrency to avoid OOMs causing pod churn. filing PR for warmup controller: https://git.redwood/warmup/PR-314

raj: preliminary RCA notes to capture in incident doc: 
- trigger: cache-invalidator event + traffic surge
- immediate cause: nodepool GPU quota exhausted -> scheduler no-sched -> warmup backlog -> requests queued -> client 5xx
- contributing: HPA maxed out, warmup init times increased due to cold KV-cache, cloud quota limits prevented node autoscaler from adding capacity

maria: we'll transition to full RCA in postmortem channel after stabilizing. For now keep this thread for in-incident coordination and timeline scratchpad.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to medium at ts=2034568200. continued monitoring for 2h.

maria: thanks all. I'll stay on until queue <100 and pending_warmups <5.

raj: thanks team — saving logs and timeline to the incident binder. followups: quota request, warmup controller PR, rollout cache guidelines.

(End of thread)
